everyday_definition: The people or organizations whose choices the model is tracking.
why_word_exists: The word keeps the model honest about who can act. If the real decision maker is missing, the rest of the analysis may solve the wrong problem.
beginner_mistake: Do not assume a player is always one person. A firm, platform, government, algorithm, bidder, or group can be a player if the model treats it as one chooser.

everyday_definition: The moves a player can actually choose inside the model.
why_word_exists: The word separates what someone wants from what someone can do. A model cannot explain choice until the available moves are clear.
beginner_mistake: Do not include imaginary options just because they would be nice, and do not omit real options because they make the model harder.

everyday_definition: A full plan for what a player would do whenever the model asks that player to choose.
why_word_exists: A single visible move is too small in games with timing, surprises, or hidden information. The plan has to say what would happen off the main path too.
beginner_mistake: Do not confuse the move that happened with the whole strategy. The unused branches often decide whether a threat or promise is credible.

everyday_definition: The score the model uses to say how much a player likes one outcome compared with another.
why_word_exists: The word turns wants into something that can be compared. Without a comparison, the model cannot say which action is better.
beginner_mistake: Do not treat payoff as full human happiness or moral worth. It is the scoreboard chosen for this model.

everyday_definition: A player's disciplined guess about something they do not directly know.
why_word_exists: Hidden information still affects choices. Beliefs let the model say how a player acts when quality, type, value, or intention is uncertain.
beginner_mistake: Do not treat a belief as a fact. It is a probability story from the player's point of view.

everyday_definition: The move that works best for one player after holding the other players' behavior fixed.
why_word_exists: Strategic choice is conditional. The same move can be smart against one rival action and foolish against another.
beginner_mistake: Do not call something a best response without saying what it is responding to.

everyday_definition: A pattern where each player's choice makes sense given the choices around it.
why_word_exists: The word closes the reasoning loop. My action fits yours, your action fits mine, and nobody has a profitable one-person move away under the stated rules.
beginner_mistake: Do not read equilibrium as good, fair, efficient, inevitable, or easy to find. It is a stability check.

everyday_definition: One move is safely worse because another move does at least as well in every relevant case and better somewhere.
why_word_exists: The word gives a justified way to remove bad choices before solving the whole game.
beginner_mistake: Do not delete a move just because it looks unlikely. Dominance needs the all-cases comparison.

everyday_definition: A planned lottery over actions, often used so the player is not easy to exploit.
why_word_exists: Some games punish predictable choices. Probabilities can be the stable object when no single fixed action works.
beginner_mistake: Do not think mixing means the player is confused. The randomness can be the strategy.

everyday_definition: A promise or threat is credible when it will still be worth carrying out later.
why_word_exists: Time separates what someone wants others to believe now from what that person will want to do when the later moment arrives.
beginner_mistake: Do not treat an announced threat as real until the later incentive has been checked.

everyday_definition: A continuation problem that starts after some history and can be analyzed as its own smaller game.
why_word_exists: The word lets the model test whether a plan remains sensible after earlier choices have already happened.
beginner_mistake: Do not assume every branch is a subgame. The players must know enough at that point for the continuation problem to stand on its own.

everyday_definition: Counting future payoffs, usually with less weight than payoffs today.
why_word_exists: Repeated games need a way to compare a gain now with rewards or punishments later.
beginner_mistake: Do not say the future disciplines behavior unless the future is valuable enough to change today's comparison.

everyday_definition: A hidden fact about a player that changes what they want, know, or can profitably do.
why_word_exists: The word lets the model handle private information without pretending everyone is the same.
beginner_mistake: Do not treat a type as a personality label. It is the private feature that matters for this model.

everyday_definition: An action or fact that changes what others believe about hidden information.
why_word_exists: When people cannot directly observe type or quality, they may infer it from costly or visible behavior.
beginner_mistake: Do not assume every message is a useful signal. A signal works only if the wrong type cannot cheaply copy it.

everyday_definition: Designing choices so different hidden types sort themselves by what they pick.
why_word_exists: The uninformed side often cannot ask for truth directly. A menu can reveal information through incentives.
beginner_mistake: Do not call a menu screening unless different types really prefer different options under the rule.

everyday_definition: A rule that uses bids to decide who gets something and what gets paid.
why_word_exists: The word names a compact setting where values, information, rules, and incentives all interact.
beginner_mistake: Do not interpret a bid before checking the payment rule, value environment, and information available to bidders.

everyday_definition: A rule system designed while expecting people to respond strategically.
why_word_exists: Some problems are not only about predicting behavior. They are about building rules that still work when people adapt.
beginner_mistake: Do not judge a mechanism by what would happen if everyone behaved nicely. Judge it by the incentives it creates.

everyday_definition: A costless, nonbinding message that may or may not change beliefs.
why_word_exists: Words can matter in games, but only when incentives make the message useful to the receiver.
beginner_mistake: Do not assume a message is informative just because it is clear. Ask why the sender would not lie.

everyday_definition: A fact everyone knows, everyone knows everyone knows, and so on.
why_word_exists: Some coordination problems require more than private awareness. People may need shared confidence that others saw the same thing.
beginner_mistake: Do not confuse many people knowing something with common knowledge. The recursive shared-awareness part is the point.

everyday_definition: A way of scoring outcomes for a group, planner, or society rather than only one player.
why_word_exists: A stable outcome can be bad for the group. Welfare language lets the reader separate private incentives from broader evaluation.
beginner_mistake: Do not assume the welfare score is neutral. Someone chose what counts and whose interests enter.
